components.name: Core Floorplan Block
components.description: 37x34 px core block with a 3 px copper voltage bar and a copper outline on the hottest core.

narrative.overview: ZenVF shows the CPU as a physical die: cores are blocks on CCD rows, voltage is copper, and charts are figure plates taken from the same die. The surface is a working measurement bench with standard Windows controls, hairline rules and no nested cards.
keyCharacteristics: Silicon and ceramic grounds with copper voltage and oxide-teal measurement.
Hairline-ruled sections; no nested cards or rounded dashboard shells.
Monospaced measurements; sans prose; Bahnschrift only for plate codes.
One signature move: the per-core floorplan.
Familiar Windows controls and window chrome.

rules.name: The Copper Is Voltage Rule
rules.body: Copper appears only where a voltage is encoded: floorplan bars, the hottest core, and the voltage series.

rules.name: The Accent Does Work Rule
rules.body: The accent marks action, selection and focus; it never tints whole sections.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: Measured values and core/CCD indices use Cascadia Mono; prose and buttons never do.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: A heading carries itself; no small all-caps kicker sits above it.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat; only the floating chart hover card carries a shadow.

dos: Do keep copper for voltage and the accent for action, selection and focus.
Do keep the floorplan in topology order and preserve core IDs.
Do use hairlines and tonal layers instead of cards.
Do keep standard Windows chrome and controls.
donts: Don't nest cards or rebuild the rail as rounded panels.
Don't use gradient text, glass, glow or colored left borders.
Don't use Bahnschrift or large display type for UI labels.
Don't put an eyebrow above a heading.
Don't encode voltage with the user accent.
